listBibl.bibl: Felix Liebermann, Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen, vol. 1 (Halle: Niemeyer, 1903), p. 530

A semi-literal English rendering of the Latin text, created for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model made by Anthropic. It is a crib to help the reader with the Latin, and should not be treated as a separate translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: Quadr Ded 14
div.ab: Patere me nostræ desperationis et sepe mecum succensende presumptionis incommoda propensius intimare!
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 530 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: Suffer me to make known more freely the troubles of our despair and of my presumption, often to be resented [?] along with me!
